More detail in [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

Listen: live fr/en transcript of a real conversation through Gemini Live in text mode, Gradium STT plus /api/translate as fallback, learn step through /api/extract, see [docs/LISTEN.md](docs/LISTEN.md).

### Offline mode (Gemma 3 1B on device)

The cloud path stays the default. When the browser is offline, or a POST to `/api/turn` or `/api/correct` fails with a network error (fetch rejects, not a 4xx/5xx), the client answers with Gemma 3 1B instruct running in the browser through the MediaPipe LLM Inference API (`@mediapipe/tasks-genai`). Replies from the device carry `source: "local"` and Roleplay shows "offline, noé runs on this device".

What works offline:

| Works | Does not |
|---|---|
| Text roleplay with Noé (typed, no Live voice, no Gradium) | Scene parsing from the camera; Look says "camera needs the network" and offers saved scenes |
| Corrections after the exchange | Gemini Live voice |
| Review and recall, the diary, kept phrases (localStorage) | |

Setup, once per browser:

1. On Hugging Face, open `litert-community/Gemma3-1B-IT`, accept the Gemma licence (the repo is gated) and download `gemma3-1b-it-int4-web.task` (about 700 MB).
2. In alltag, open Settings, section "offline tutor", and choose that file. It is copied into the Origin Private File System and loaded from there; the app never downloads it on its own.
3. Optional: set `VITE_GEMMA_MODEL_URL` to a URL you host the file at; Settings then shows a "download" button instead of the file picker.

Requirements and caveats: needs WebGPU (current Chrome or Edge on desktop or Android) and OPFS; elsewhere Settings says "not supported". The MediaPipe LLM Inference web API is in maintenance mode upstream; fine for a hackathon demo, not a long-term bet. A 1B model is much weaker than the cloud models: prompts are short and French, and its JSON is parsed leniently with safe defaults.

#### Bundled in the iOS app

The native app ships the model in its bundle, so a TestFlight or App Store install has the offline tutor ready with no file picking.

```sh
pnpm model:fetch      # scripts/fetch-model.sh: hf CLI, or curl with HF_TOKEN; into public/models/
pnpm ios:build        # warns (does not fail) when public/models has no .task file
```

- `public/models/gemma3-1b-it-int4-web.task` lands in `dist/` and is served at `https://localhost/models/...` inside the app. On start `src/offline/gemma.ts` sends a HEAD there; a 200 loads the model straight from that URL and Settings shows "ready, built into the app".
- The file ships inside the IPA (about 700 MB), so the App Store marks the app as a large download.
- It is not in git, not deployed to Vercel and never precached by the service worker; the web app keeps the file picker.
- Licence: Gemma is distributed under the [Gemma Terms of Use](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/terms). The app must show that notice and link the [prohibited use policy](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/prohibited_use_policy); Settings shows "on-device model: Gemma 3 1B, Gemma Terms of Use" whenever a model is bundled or installed.
- Later: Apple Background Assets essential downloads fetch the model from our own host during App Store installation, so the IPA stays small and the model is still there on first launch.

#### Install on your phone

The app ships a service worker, so once installed it opens with no network and the offline tutor is reachable.

- Android Chrome: open the site, then Settings, "on your phone", "add to home screen" (or the browser menu, "Add to home screen").

#!/bin/sh
# Downloads the Gemma 4 E2B web model into public/models/ so the native app ships it.
# Uses the hf CLI when present, else curl. The repo is not gated; HF_TOKEN is optional.
set -eu

REPO="litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm"
FILE="gemma-4-E2B-it-web.task"
DIR="public/models"
MIN_BYTES=1500000000

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

echo "Gemma 4 is released under Apache 2.0: https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0"
echo "Model: https://huggingface.co/$REPO (about 2 GB)"
echo

mkdir -p "$DIR"

if command -v hf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  hf download "$REPO" "$FILE" --local-dir "$DIR"
elif [ -n "${HF_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  # The header comes from stdin so the token never shows up in ps or in the output.
  printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\n' "$HF_TOKEN" |
    curl -fL --progress-bar -H @- -o "$DIR/$FILE.part" \
      "https://huggingface.co/$REPO/resolve/main/$FILE"
  mv "$DIR/$FILE.part" "$DIR/$FILE"
else
  curl -fL --progress-bar -o "$DIR/$FILE.part" \
    "https://huggingface.co/$REPO/resolve/main/$FILE"
  mv "$DIR/$FILE.part" "$DIR/$FILE"
fi

size=$(wc -c < "$DIR/$FILE" | tr -d ' ')
if [ "$size" -le "$MIN_BYTES" ]; then
  echo "error: $DIR/$FILE is $size bytes, expected more than 1500 MB" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "ok: $DIR/$FILE ($size bytes)"
EOF
sh -n scripts/fetch-model.sh && echo syntax ok

- Fetch it: `pnpm model:fetch` (runs `scripts/fetch-model.sh`; uses the `hf` CLI if installed, else curl). The repo is not gated, so no token is needed; `HF_TOKEN` is used if set.

Licence: Gemma 4 is released under [Apache 2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0). Settings shows "on-device model: Gemma 4 E2B, Apache 2.0" in the offline tutor section.
EOF

#!/bin/sh
# Downloads the Gemma 4 E2B web model into public/models/ so the native app ships it.
# Uses the hf CLI when present, else curl. The repo is not gated; HF_TOKEN is optional.
set -eu

REPO="litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm"
FILE="gemma-4-E2B-it-web.task"
DIR="public/models"
MIN_BYTES=1500000000

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

echo "Gemma 4 is released under Apache 2.0: https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0"
echo "Model: https://huggingface.co/$REPO (about 2 GB)"
echo

mkdir -p "$DIR"

if command -v hf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  hf download "$REPO" "$FILE" --local-dir "$DIR"
elif [ -n "${HF_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  # The header comes from stdin so the token never shows up in ps or in the output.
  printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\n' "$HF_TOKEN" |
    curl -fL --progress-bar -H @- -o "$DIR/$FILE.part" \
      "https://huggingface.co/$REPO/resolve/main/$FILE"
  mv "$DIR/$FILE.part" "$DIR/$FILE"
else
  curl -fL --progress-bar -o "$DIR/$FILE.part" \
    "https://huggingface.co/$REPO/resolve/main/$FILE"
  mv "$DIR/$FILE.part" "$DIR/$FILE"
fi

size=$(wc -c < "$DIR/$FILE" | tr -d ' ')
if [ "$size" -le "$MIN_BYTES" ]; then
  echo "error: $DIR/$FILE is $size bytes, expected more than 1500 MB" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "ok: $DIR/$FILE ($size bytes)"

What alltag teaches today, what the stack underneath could carry, and what adding a language takes. Researched 2026-10-10 from the Gradium docs, the Gemini Live guide and the Gemma 4 model card.

## Today

The app teaches French only. The target language is fixed in settings and in the prompts (Noé, review, Listen, the offline prompts); there is no picker.

## What the stack supports

Three tiers, from the full experience down to offline text.

### A. Full experience with Gradium voice

English (`en`), French (`fr`), German (`de`), Spanish (`es`), Portuguese (`pt`), plus the Swiss French (`fr-ch`) and Swiss German accents of the Gradium voice library.

Gradium voice persona, Gradium STT for review, `/api/translate` and Gemini on top. Gradium transcription accepts only these five languages (or `any`); more are announced.

### B. Gemini only: voice and transcription

Gemini Live native audio voice, input transcription, vision and grading, with no Gradium voice. The Live API and its input transcription cover the 99 languages below. Native audio output has 30 HD voices in 24 languages (no per-language list published), so expect the best voice quality in those.

| Language | Code |
|---|---|
"""
tail="""
### C. Offline: Gemma 4 E2B on device

Gemma 4 E2B (`src/offline/gemma.ts`, Apache 2.0) is pretrained on 140+ languages with out-of-the-box support for 35+. The model card has no per-language list. On the web it is text only and needs WebGPU: typed roleplay and corrections, no voice, no camera.

## What it takes to add a language

1. Settings: a target language field (stored with the other settings) instead of the fixed French.
2. Prompts: pass the language as a parameter to every prompt (Noé, corrections, review, Listen translate and extract, the offline prompts in `src/offline/prompts.ts`) instead of hard-coded French.
3. Tier A only: route Gradium voice and STT to that language and pick a voice or accent from the library.
4. Tier B: Gemini Live voice and Gemini TTS for that language, with the Gemini Live transcription language set to match; no Gradium.
5. Onboarding: a language picker on first run, limited to the languages wired up so far.
"""
